findings.subject: Operations
findings.title: Database connection open, begin-transaction, commit/rollback and close are synchronous in an async request path

evidence.excerpt: var connection = CreateConnection(...); if (connection.State != ConnectionState.Open) { connection.Open(); } var transaction = connection.BeginTransaction();

findings.recommendation: Create the connection as DbConnection, use await OpenAsync(cancellationToken), await BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync/RollbackAsync and dispose with await using, so no thread-pool thread blocks on network I/O.

strengths.title: Async/await and CancellationToken propagated from controller through service to Dapper command

evidence.excerpt: public async Task<IActionResult> ResetTesting(CancellationToken cancellationToken) { var response = await testingService.ResetTestingAsync(cancellationToken);

strengths.subject: Operations
strengths.title: Entire reset is a single batched SQL script per call, avoiding per-table round trips

checkResults.subject: Operations
checkResults.reason: No expensive or repeated read operations exist; the only data operation is a destructive reset and the other endpoints return static/config values.

checkResults.subject: Operations
checkResults.reason: Connection Open, BeginTransaction, Commit/Rollback and Close are blocking synchronous calls inside an async method.

notes: PERF-03 passes because ADO.NET pooling is on by default (connection strings do not disable it). Minor related hygiene: the connection/transaction are not disposed via using, so an exception between Open and the inner try would leave the connection unreturned to the pool; ApiExtensions calls BuildServiceProvider() at startup (extra container, startup-only).
